newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures soar to huge daily gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures soar to huge daily gains.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures soared to huge daily gains in a widespread rally that resulted in some of the biggest single-day point gains ever.

The Standard & Poor's 500 index closed up 21.09 points at 794.05, its second biggest closing gain since the broad-based benchmark index closed up 21.55 points on October 21, 1987, according to Standard & Poor's data.

S&P 500 futures settled up 24.60 points at 799.80. Floor brokers said the futures rise was among the two or three biggest daily gains ever, although the Chicago Mercantile Exchange does not keep track of daily net point changes.
"I've been in S&Ps for many years, and I'd say this is one of the biggest," said one S&P 500 futures broker of the day's net point gain. "This is comparable (to cash S&Ps)."
Activity swelled again late on an influx of dealer and local buying that emerged after U.S. Treasury bond futures closed with point-plus gains and near day's peaks.
"It was straight up, good aggressive buying," said the broker.
He also noted signs that arbitrageurs were executing buy programs manually, without use of the New York Stock Exchange's computer.
The NYSE's index arb curb kicked in hours earlier when the Dow 30 Industrial index had risen 50 points.

The rally in nearby S&P 500s, which occurred on volume estimated on the price boards at about 80,000 June futures, rammed into a ceiling at 800.00, the day's peak and considered a key resistance level.

At the same time, cash S&P 500s stalled near 795.00, solid resistance hit on the March 3 price "valley" formed between the February 19 and March 11 peaks, according to Jay Hohmann, head futures trader, Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.
Some brokers said the rise, which some said may have lifted futures closer to overbought territory, might be overextended and vulnerable to a small setback soon.
"I'm skeptical," said the floor broker. "It just seems a little overdone, a little overinflated. I wouldn't be surprised to see this thing come back down."
He pegged interim support at 796.00 for nearby S&P 500s.

Futures romped higher before pit trading opened, surging from small overnight losses after T-bond futures soared on weaker than expected U.S. economic data that analysts said made them rethink the need for more credit tightening.
The first-quarter U.S. employment cost index rose 0.6 percent compared to expectations for a 0.9 percent increase.
March U.S. durable goods orders fell 3.0 percent versus forecasts for no change in the volatile measure.
The Conference Board said consumer confidence in April slipped to 116.8 against forecasts for 118.4.
Traders said remarks by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan at the IMF/World Bank meeting had little effect.

June S&Ps rose 24.60 to 799.80, Value Lines up 17.30 to 700.50, Nikkei up 225.0 at 18,875.0, Midcap up 6.70 at 257.70, Russell rose 6.35 to 344.25, Nasdaq rose 29.00 to 865.75. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
